source_text: Κείσθω δέ σοι πάντα εἰς θεὸν καὶ ἔργα καὶ λόγοι, καὶ πάντα ἀνάφερε Χριστῷ τὰ σαυτοῦ, καὶ πυκνῶς ἐπὶ θεὸν τρέπε τὴν ψυχήν, καὶ τὸ νόημα ἐπέρειδε τῇ Χριστοῦ δυνάμει ὥσπερ ἐν λιμένι τινὶ τῷ θείῳ φωτὶ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἀναπαυόμενον ἀπὸ πάσης λαλιᾶς τε καὶ πράξεως. καὶ μεθ’ ἡμέραν πολλάκις μὲν ἀνθρώποις κοίνου τὴν σεαυτοῦ φρόνησιν, θεῷ δὲ ἐπὶ πλεῖστον ἐν νυκτὶ ὁμοίως καὶ ἐν ἡμέρᾳ· μὴ γὰρ ὕπνος σε ἐπικρατείτω πολὺς τῶν πρὸς θεὸν εὐχῶν τε καὶ ὕμνων· θανάτῳ γὰρ ὁ μακρὸς ὕπνος ἐφάμιλλος. μέτοχος Χριστοῦ ἀεὶ καθίστασο τοῦ τὴν θείαν αὐγὴν καταλάμποντος ἐξ οὐρανοῦ· εὐφροσύνη γὰρ ἔστω σοι διηνεκὴς καὶ ἄπαυστος ὁ Χριστός.
thought_title: Directing all words and deeds to God and Christ
orientation: Clement continues his direct address to the newly baptized, now turning from rules of speech and conduct to the constant orientation of the soul toward God and Christ.
pass_a_gloss: Let all things be laid by you toward God, both works and words, and refer all your own things up to Christ, and frequently turn the soul toward God, and prop the thought upon the power of Christ, as in some harbor resting in the divine light of the Savior from all talk and action. And after the day, share your own wisdom often with humans, but with God most of all in night likewise and in day; for let not much sleep overpower you, away from prayers and hymns toward God; for long sleep is a match for death. Always make yourself a partaker of Christ, who shines the divine ray from heaven; for let Christ be to you a perpetual and unceasing joy.

choices.term: Κείσθω δέ σοι πάντα εἰς θεὸν καὶ ἔργα καὶ λόγοι
choices.english: Let all things be laid by you toward God, both works and words
choices.why: The passive imperative κείσθω with dative σοι keeps the sense of the believer laying all things before God as an offering or deposit; 'toward God' preserves the directional force of εἰς θεόν.
rejected: Let all your works and words be directed to God
Let everything you do and say be for God

choices.english: refer all your own things up to Christ
choices.why: ἀναφέρω has the sense of bringing or referring something up to a higher authority; 'refer up' keeps the upward motion and the idea of entrusting one's affairs to Christ.

choices.english: prop the thought upon the power of Christ
choices.why: ἐπερείδω means to rest or lean something upon a support; 'prop' conveys the firm resting of the mind on Christ's power as a foundation.
rejected: fix your thought on the power of Christ
lean your mind on Christ's power

choices.term: ὥσπερ ἐν λιμένι τινὶ τῷ θείῳ φωτὶ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἀναπαυόμενον
choices.english: as in some harbor resting in the divine light of the Savior
choices.why: The simile of a harbor is explicit in the Greek; 'some harbor' preserves the indefinite τινὶ, and 'resting in the divine light' keeps the participial phrase attached to the thought.
rejected: as in a harbor, resting in the Savior's divine light
like a harbor where you rest in the divine light of the Savior

choices.term: θανάτῳ γὰρ ὁ μακρὸς ὕπνος ἐφάμιλλος
choices.english: for long sleep is a match for death
choices.why: ἐφάμιλλος means 'rival to' or 'comparable to'; 'a match for' conveys the sense that long sleep rivals death in its effect of cutting one off from prayer and hymns.
rejected: long sleep is equal to death

choices.english: Always make yourself a partaker of Christ
choices.why: καθίστασο is a middle imperative meaning 'establish yourself' or 'make yourself'; 'make yourself a partaker' keeps the active self-positioning and the sense of ongoing participation.
rejected: always be a partaker of Christ
always become a sharer in Christ

pass_b_english: Let all your works and words be laid before God, and refer everything of yours up to Christ. Turn your soul frequently to God, and rest your thought upon the power of Christ as in a harbor, resting in the divine light of the Savior from all talk and action. During the day, share your wisdom often with people, but be with God as much as possible at night and in the day alike. Do not let long sleep overpower your prayers and hymns to God, for long sleep is a match for death. Always make yourself a partaker of Christ, who shines the divine brightness down from heaven. Let Christ be your perpetual and unceasing joy.

last_rejected.quote: rest your thought upon the power of Christ
last_rejected.source_quote: τὸ νόημα ἐπέρειδε τῇ Χριστοῦ δυνάμει
last_rejected.why: Greek says ‘strengthen the mind’, not ‘rest the thought’
last_rejected.fix: strengthen your mind with the power of Christ
last_rejected.ruling: ἐπέρειδε means 'lean/rest upon'; 'rest upon' is valid, not 'strengthen'

last_rejected.quote: Do not let long sleep overpower your prayers and hymns to God
last_rejected.why: ‘long’ is not in the Greek clause about sleep domination
last_rejected.fix: Do not let sleep overpower your prayers and hymns to God
last_rejected.ruling: πολὺς modifies ὕπνος in same clause; 'long sleep' is accurate, not addition
